To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

health worker migration theories have traditionally tended to focus on labor market conditions as push or pull factors, and have not adequately addressed the role of education systems and global marketization in the production of globally oriented health workers, and that global political economy (or GPE) is an appropriate theoretical perspective to highlight the increasing interlinkage of educational investment and global tendencies of health worker migration in India, and to inform a broader understanding of health worker migration and the marketization of education and health systems in the country.
the marketization of health education is a global phenomenon and is a key contributor to the migration of health professionals.

the international migration of health workers from India has been driven by the marketization and privatisation of health care and health education in India, and that these tendencies reflect a broader process of marketization and privitisation of education and health in India.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the marketization of Indian health care education in the production of globally oriented health care professionals.
the global political economy of education, health care and health worker migration, which is a neglected area of scholarship.
how the Indian health care system is being reformed and the implications of such reforms for the health care system and the health of the population.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Indian health care education system has become a key part of the global political economy of health worker production and migration.
global political economy provides a useful perspective to understanding the role of education in the migration of health workers.
the GPE approach is a useful framework that can be used in the analysis of health worker migration.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the Indian case illustrates how the global orientation and marketization of health care training is increasingly central to understanding the place of health professionals in global and Asian migration.
the global political economy of health worker migration is a complex and dynamic one, which is increasingly driven by the global orientation of health education systems.

the Indian case demonstrates the need for a more comprehensive understanding of health worker migration that is sensitive to the global political economy of health care education, and the ways in which this is changing in response to the global migration of health workers.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the global orientation of health education systems is a central feature of health worker migration and that the global political economy perspective is well suited to understanding these tendencies.
the production of health workers for the international labour market is increasingly a key component of the global political economy of health education.
the GPE perspective provides an important framework for understanding the role of education and training in the migration of health workers.
